review_comment:
Simply subtracting two integers is discouraged. Instead, `Integer.compare` is recommended.

I think it doesn't matter in this case, because the range of these two values is so limited, but it might be best to call `Integer.compare` so the code doesn't "look wrong".

Using `charAt` tends to cause problems for characters outside the basic multilingual plane (like emojis), but I suspect it doesn't matter in this case because we're only comparing for order, not trying to identify the actual characters.

As silly as it sounds, it might be good to have at least one test with an emoji to demonstrate that this logic works with characters outside the BMP.

I added a test and there were no surprises.
I think we are OK here: as you said, as long as the order is consistent we don't care much. One important caveat is that we do not match the "special" char (/ or \) with a random surrogate by mistake, but surrogates are in a whole different range, so that won't be an issue.
